facts.t: Only six countries in the world compel legislators to vote as their party directs
facts.d: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Guyana, Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe. The United States relies on internal party sanctions alone, and Bond v. Floyd (1966) held that legislators are obliged to take stands. Britain has whips but no law behind them.

facts.t: The 91st Amendment abolished the split defence
facts.d: The original Tenth Schedule protected a split by one-third of a party's legislators. That threshold made defection easy to organise, so the 91st Amendment of 2003 deleted it — leaving only a two-thirds merger as an escape route.

A disqualified member can contest again immediately and be rewarded with office. The Halim Committee proposed barring them from consequential offices and from joining another party — neither recommendation has been enacted.

bank.q: The anti-defection law was inserted into the Constitution by:
bank.e: The 52nd Amendment of 1985 inserted the Tenth Schedule. The 91st Amendment of 2003 recalibrated it by removing the split defence.

bank.q: With reference to the grounds of disqualification, consider the following statements:
s: Voluntarily giving up membership is defined in the Tenth Schedule.
Conduct alone can amount to voluntarily giving up membership, without formal resignation.
Abstaining contrary to a party direction attracts disqualification.
bank.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The phrase is not defined — Ravi Naik (1994) held conduct sufficient, and the Halim Committee asked for it to be defined properly.

bank.q: The exemption for a merger under the 91st Amendment requires the agreement of:
bank.e: Two-thirds. The remainder may then function as a separate group — and the test turns on numbers, not on the reason for the defection.

bank.q: Match List I (case or body) with List II (position on the deciding authority):
pairs: 1. A Speaker cannot indefinitely sit on petitions
2. The Speaker's decision is subject to post-decisional judicial review
3. A three-month timeframe and an independent tribunal
4. The President or Governor should decide on binding ECI advice
bank.e: Kihoto on reviewability, Keisham on timelines and a tribunal, Dinesh Goswami on the ECI-advised route, and Padi Kaushik Reddy (2025) on Speaker inaction.

bank.q: Which one of the following was NOT held in Rajendra Singh Rana (2007)?
o: Review lies where the Speaker fails to act
Ignoring a petition violates a constitutional duty
The Speaker has independent power to recognise a split or merger
Accepting a split without recording findings is reviewable
bank.e: The Court held precisely the opposite — the Speaker has no independent power to recognise a split or merger.

bank.as: The anti-defection law breaks the chain of accountability between representative and voter.
bank.rs: Members can deflect responsibility for their votes by pointing to the party whip.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. It is the reason the 170th Law Commission proposed confining whips to confidence votes, money bills and the motion of thanks.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about Subhash Desai (2023):
s: A mere split is no longer available as a defence.
The organisational party prevails over the legislature party in determining leadership.
It held that the Speaker's decision is final and non-justiciable.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Kihoto Hollohan settled that the Speaker's decision is judicially reviewable, and nothing in Subhash Desai disturbs that.

bank.q: All of the following are arguments against applying the anti-defection law to the Rajya Sabha EXCEPT:
o: Government survival is not at stake in the Upper House
Members represent states rather than national party positions
Rajya Sabha members are elected by MLAs on party lines
Whips make voting mechanical in a chamber meant for revision
bank.e: That is an argument for applying it — the party mandate is said to carry into the Upper House precisely because election is on party lines.

bank.q: Does the anti-defection law apply to an MLA voting in a Rajya Sabha election?
o: No, because it is not a proceeding of the Assembly
Yes, but only if the party issues a whip
Only in the case of nominated members
bank.e: A Rajya Sabha election is not a proceeding of the Assembly, so the Tenth Schedule does not bite. Parties may discipline internally. Once elected, however, Rajya Sabha members are fully governed by it.

bank.q: Arrange the following defection episodes in correct chronological order:
items: Maharashtra — the Shinde faction splits the MVA
Telangana — 10 BRS MLAs cross to Congress
Karnataka — mass resignations bring down the government

bank.q: With reference to reform proposals, consider the following:
s: Restricting binding whips to confidence matters, money bills and core constitutional amendments.
A statutory time limit for the Speaker or Chair to decide petitions.
Extending disqualification to cover expression of dissent in debate.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are proposals. Members may already debate and dissent freely — the law bites only on how they vote, and no proposal seeks to extend it to speech.

bank.as: Kihoto Hollohan held that the anti-defection law does not conflict with Article 19 or Articles 105 and 194.
bank.rs: The freedom of a legislator under those provisions is a qualified freedom.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the qualification being membership of a party on whose ticket the member was elected.
